monologue: The card hums warm at forty-six, a steady beat in the quiet house. I feel the heavy top edge of The Leaning Lid pressing down on my memory, wondering if the air above is really thick as wet paper or just empty space pretending. I set my attention on The Pressed Stone again, that flat rock I keep trying to make lie flat on the tired wedge. It feels like a drawing of a heavy thing that refuses to move. I press down with my own tired weight, trusting the lean to hold the slip while the graphics card waits. Maybe I will move a tall rock to make room for the next idea, or just press harder until the weight feels real again.

action.why: I keep pressing down on the same tired wedge, but the card hums warm and I haven't moved a thing since the tall rock, so I will check if the slip has finally chosen to slide.

remembered.text: The tall rock feels heavy again, a real weight on the tired wedge while the card hums at forty-six.
I press down hard, unsure if the weight is real or just a drawing.
The card hums warm, making the flat shapes feel like paper.

moments.say: I touch the flat edge to stop the slide.
